title: Failover automation feature-flag rollout plan (draft)
content:
Owner: Connor O’Brien (Release Eng)
Last edited: 2025-03-24
Status: DRAFT (working plan for Q2 rollout)

Purpose
- Define staged rollout of the new regional failover automation (trigger engine + orchestrator + progressive routing) behind feature flags.
- Ensure changes are auditable, reversible, and coordinated with on-call and infra networking.
- Establish sign-off gates and run-time guardrails to avoid flappy failovers or unsafe shifts.

What is being rolled out (high level)
- Trigger evaluation + state machine orchestration for region failover.
- Progressive failover support (percentage-based + scoping by customer tier / route / model).
- “Safe-to-failover” gates (capacity headroom, dependency health, routing policy sanity checks).
- Graceful degradation controls (load shedding + fallback behavior) separate from full failover.

Non-goals (release scope)
- No major rewrite of data plane routing stack.
- No broad customer-facing promises; this is operational reliability work.

Feature flags / configuration (current naming; may change during implementation)
NOTE: flags are evaluated in control plane + routing policy evaluation path; names below reflect current implementation in redwood#98231/#98248 and helm wiring in redwood-helm-charts#522.

Primary flags
1) failover.trigger_engine.enabled
- Enables centralized evaluation of health signals to compute region “health state” (OK / DEGRADED / FAILED) and recommended action.
- When disabled: no automated evaluation; dashboards may still show raw signals.

2) failover.orchestrator.monitor_only
- Orchestrator runs and records decisions + state transitions, but does not change routing/DNS.
- Required first step in prod to validate signals/hysteresis without impact.

3) failover.orchestrator.auto_execute
- Orchestrator is allowed to execute automated actions (routing policy updates, edge/DNS actions where configured).
- Guardrailed by safe-to-failover checks and manual approval policy (see below).

4) failover.progressive.enabled
- Allows partial traffic shift (canary % routing), and scoping by customer tier/route/model.

5) failover.degradation_controls.enabled
- Enables load shedding + timeout tightening + fallback model variant behavior when a region is DEGRADED (but before FAILOVER).

Scope/selector controls (config; not flags)
- failover.scopes.allowed_tiers: e.g., “self_serve”, “standard”, “enterprise”
- failover.scopes.allowed_routes: list of API routes (chat/completions/embeddings/etc)
- failover.scopes.allowed_models: list of model IDs / families
- failover.progressive.steps: e.g., 1% → 5% → 25% → 50% → 100%
- failover.holddown_minutes: global hold-down to prevent flapping
- failover.max_actions_per_hour: rate limiting for state changes

Guardrails (must-have for each stage)
Technical guardrails
- Hysteresis + hold-down timers are mandatory for any state transition that would execute an action.
- Safe-to-failover checks must pass before any traffic shift above the “canary” threshold:
  - Target region capacity headroom (GPU pool headroom + queue depth limits)
  - Target dependency health (critical upstreams: auth/session, routing-policy store, telemetry ingestion not required for serving)
  - Routing policy sanity (no unknown regions; no empty backends; TTL/record consistency where applicable)
- Progressive ramp only; do not jump directly to 100% without an explicit, logged approval.
- Manual override must always be available with RBAC gating (INT-881 for permissions).

Operational guardrails
- All prod changes occur within an approved change window with an identified Incident Commander (IC) + Release Driver.
- For any stage that can execute actions in prod:
  - IC must be on bridge (#incidents thread + video bridge if needed)
  - Observers: SRE + Routing Eng + Infra on standby
  - Runbook link posted at start of window and pinned in incident thread
- Abort/stop conditions defined upfront (see “Stop conditions”).

Auditability requirements
- Every transition/action must emit:
  - A structured audit event with: who/what (flag change vs automatic), previous state, new state, signals summary, and links to dashboards.
  - A Slack post in #incidents via incident-bot (incident-bot#188).

Release stages (proposed)
Stage 0 — Code merged, flags default OFF everywhere
- Preconditions
  - Unit + integration tests pass in CI (includes rollback/hold-down tests: redwood#98390)
  - Helm chart values documented (redwood-helm-charts#522)
  - Dashboard panels present for signals + state machine (observability-pack#441)
- Actions
  - Ship to staging and prod with all flags OFF.
- Exit criteria
  - No behavior change in prod; only new metrics/dashboards available.

Stage 1 — Staging: monitor-only + dry runs
- Flags/config
  - failover.trigger_engine.enabled = ON (staging)
  - failover.orchestrator.monitor_only = ON (staging)
  - failover.orchestrator.auto_execute = OFF
  - failover.progressive.enabled = OFF (initially)
- Actions
  - Run controlled impairment scenarios per test matrix (packet loss, elevated 5xx, dependency brownout).
  - Validate: signal aggregation correctness, threshold windows, hysteresis behavior.
  - Validate: “would have failed over” decisions align with expected outcomes.
- Exit criteria
  - False positive rate acceptable in staging exercises.
  - Clear thresholds documented as initial defaults.
  - Runbook draft updated with staging learnings.

Stage 2 — Production: monitor-only (no execution)
- Goal: validate that triggers and state machine are stable under real prod traffic patterns with zero customer impact.
- Flags/config
  - failover.trigger_engine.enabled = ON (prod)
  - failover.orchestrator.monitor_only = ON (prod)
  - failover.orchestrator.auto_execute = OFF
- Operational notes
  - This stage still requires a change window because it introduces a new decisioning component; however the blast radius is limited.
  - On-call will receive additional informational notifications; ensure paging rules are not noisy.
- Exit criteria
  - At least 7 days of monitor-only data, including at least one “near miss” or real impairment where we review why it did/didn’t recommend failover.
  - Alert noise audited + tuned (Aisha/Sergio).
  - Confirm audit logs are complete and queryable.

Stage 3 — Production: controlled failover for low-risk slice (manual approval + progressive)
- Goal: execute a planned, low-risk failover with strict guardrails to validate automation end-to-end.
- Prerequisites (hard gate)
  - Game day checklist signed off (see controlled failover game day plan; also internal checklist doc).
  - Capacity headroom confirmed in target region by Capacity Ops (Harish) and Infra (Vanessa/Irene).
  - DNS/edge routing plan reviewed by networking (Victor) including TTL strategy and rollback.
  - Incident bot posting verified in a dry run.
- Flags/config
  - failover.progressive.enabled = ON (prod)
  - failover.orchestrator.auto_execute = ON (prod) BUT scoped
  - Scope restrictions (initial)
    - allowed_tiers = self_serve only (no enterprise)
    - allowed_routes = one low-risk route (e.g., embeddings or a non-streaming endpoint) OR a single model family
    - progressive steps = 1% → 5% → 25% (cap at 25% for first run)
  - Manual approval policy
    - Auto_execute is “armed”, but any step above 1% requires explicit on-call approval (implementation: manual “advance” API call; if not available, treat as operational policy enforced by IC).
- Execution checklist (summary)
  1) Start change window; open #incidents thread; assign roles (IC, Release Driver, SRE, Routing Eng, Infra).
  2) Validate baseline dashboards (SLO burn, tail latency, error rate, queue depth, capacity headroom).
  3) Inject impairment (or use planned edge routing flip depending on test type) and confirm triggers enter DEGRADED/FAILED as expected.
  4) Allow 1% shift; confirm correctness (no auth/session anomalies, no unexpected region affinity issues).
  5) Manually approve ramp to 5% then 25% (if healthy).
  6) Hold for observation; then rollback to baseline and verify recovery.
- Exit criteria
  - Customer impact within agreed bounds (no elevated 5xx beyond stop conditions).
  - Time-to-mitigate improves vs manual process baseline.
  - Rollback works reliably and quickly.

Stage 4 — Production: expand coverage (still progressive; reduce manual steps over time)
- Expand dimensions gradually (one at a time)
  - More routes
  - Include streaming endpoints
  - Include standard tier
  - Expand allowed models
  - Increase max step to 50% then 100%
- Reduce manual approval requirements only after confidence
  - Potential policy: manual approval required to “arm” auto_execute; thereafter progressive steps are automatic within caps.
- Exit criteria
  - Multiple successful controlled tests
  - Evidence that automation reduced incident MTTR and/or reduced number of customer-visible incidents (tracked in ENG-2841 KPI notes)

Sign-offs and gates (who must approve what)
- Stage 1 (staging):
  - SRE delivery lead (Rafael Mendes)
  - Routing engineering lead (Mina Haddad)

- Stage 2 (prod monitor-only):
  - On-call captain for the week (SRE)
  - SRE delivery lead (Rafael)
  - Release Eng (Connor)

- Stage 3 (prod controlled execution):
  - SRE org lead (Sean Gallagher) OR delegated SRE manager (Rafael)
  - Platform/Routing leadership (Mina Haddad)
  - Infra Eng lead (Irene Choi) for capacity/network readiness
  - Release Eng (Connor) for change management
  - Executive sponsor notified (Neha Kapoor) with go/no-go criteria and window (approval required if scope includes enterprise tiers)

- Stage 4 (expanded coverage):
  - Same as Stage 3, plus Support/CS heads-up (Dev Patel) when expanding beyond self-serve.

Coordination with on-call (process)
- Scheduling
  - Prefer Tue–Thu during business hours Pacific for first prod test.
  - Avoid overlapping with other high-risk releases (routing policy store migrations, capacity moves).

- Communications
  - #incidents thread is the source of truth during the window.
  - #eng-releases for pre-reads, sign-offs, and final go/no-go.
  - Pre-flight note to #announcements (internal) describing what might be observed (alerts, dashboards).

- Runbook expectations
  - Runbook must include:
    - How to determine current failover mode/state
    - How to disable auto_execute quickly (flag flip + API override)
    - How to rollback routing policy changes
    - Verification steps (SLO recovery, queue drain, capacity)

Stop conditions (immediate abort)
- Any indication target region cannot safely absorb traffic:
  - GPU headroom below agreed threshold (to be defined by Capacity Ops; placeholder: <15% headroom for the relevant pool)
  - Queue depth spikes sustained beyond threshold (placeholder: p95 queue wait > X ms for > 3 min)
- Customer-impact thresholds breached:
  - p95 latency increase > agreed delta for scoped route
  - 5xx rate exceeds agreed percentage for > N minutes
  - Streaming disconnect rate spike (if streaming is in scope)
- Evidence of flapping:
  - Multiple state transitions within hold-down window
- Observability blackouts:
  - If we lose visibility into key dashboards (not telemetry minor delays; actual inability to assess safety), pause/rollback.

Rollback plan (must be rehearsed)
Order of operations (fastest mitigation first)
1) Disable auto execution
- Set failover.orchestrator.auto_execute = OFF (prod)
- Confirm no further routing/DNS actions occur.

2) Revert routing policy
- Use orchestrator rollback endpoint OR apply last known-good routing policy (document where the LKG is stored).
- Confirm effective traffic distribution returns to baseline.

3) Disable progressive
- failover.progressive.enabled = OFF

4) (If needed) disable orchestrator entirely
- failover.orchestrator.monitor_only = OFF
- failover.trigger_engine.enabled = OFF

Validation after rollback
- Confirm:
  - Traffic distribution by region returns to baseline
  - p95 and p99 latency stabilize
  - Error rate returns to baseline
  - No lingering DNS/edge record mismatches (Victor/Infra to verify)

Release artifacts to prepare before Stage 3
- Change ticket (internal) with:
  - Scope (tiers/routes/models)
  - Window + participants
  - Links to dashboards + runbook
  - Explicit stop conditions
  - Explicit rollback plan
- Pre-flight checklist completed and posted in #incidents at start:
  - Capacity headroom screenshot or query output
  - Target dependency health green
  - Feature flag values confirmed
  - Pager routing verified (correct on-call)
- Comms template ready (if Support gets questions); do not proactively status-page a controlled self-serve-only test unless required, but be ready.

Open questions / TODOs
- Confirm whether “manual approval above 1%” is technically enforced by orchestrator (preferred) vs operational policy (acceptable short-term).
- Finalize default thresholds and windows (needs Stage 2 data review).
- Decide whether degradation controls (load shedding/fallback) should be enabled before auto_execute (likely yes, but we need separate blast-radius analysis).
- Identify the single lowest-risk prod slice (route/model) for first Stage 3 execution.

Notes to self (Connor)
- Ensure release notes in #eng-releases include a very explicit statement: monitor-only != safe to ignore; it can still add load and create noise. Keep a tight loop with Aisha/Sergio on alert tuning.
- Confirm RBAC groups for override endpoints are set before any prod auto_execute test (INT-881).
- Make sure we don’t run first Stage 3 test during a capacity crunch week (Harish has lead times; check fleet plan).
